skill.name: deploy
skill.description: Enforces local build, browser, and test checks before running deployment commands.
skill.summary: Requires local verification before production deployment.
skill.author: ChakshuGautam

security_audit.summary: The external-command findings are real because the skill instructs agents to run package scripts, start a local server, execute tests, and perform a production Vercel deployment. The commands are consistent with the stated deployment workflow, and no prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found. Publication should require clear user confirmation before any production deployment command runs.

remediation.issue: Production deployment can run after checks without a separate confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation immediately before any production deployment command, even when the user originally asked to deploy.

remediation.issue: Package manager commands execute repository-defined scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to run this skill only in trusted repositories and review package scripts before execution.

remediation.issue: Workflow assumes pnpm, Vercel, and Chrome DevTools MCP are available.
remediation.suggestion: Document prerequisites and provide safe alternatives when a project uses different tooling.

finding_verdicts.reason: The bash block at SKILL.md lines 15-17 instructs the agent to run a package build command. This is expected for deployment checks, but package scripts can execute arbitrary project-defined commands.

The detected range is a markdown fence boundary, but it is part of the workflow that transitions from one local command to another. The surrounding instructions still direct external package-script execution.
The bash block at SKILL.md lines 22-24 instructs running the local development server through a package script. This can execute arbitrary repository-defined startup logic and open local services.
The line is a markdown fence boundary, but it belongs to the local server command block and its follow-on browser testing workflow. The external command is legitimate but still has side effects.
The bash block at SKILL.md lines 36-38 instructs running project tests through the package manager. Test scripts are useful but can execute arbitrary commands from the repository.

The detected markdown fence sits immediately before the production deployment section. The workflow continues into external deployment command execution, so the risk is real even though the fence itself is not Ruby execution.

The bash block at SKILL.md lines 42-44 instructs running a production Vercel deployment command. That command can publish code and make networked production changes, so it requires explicit user control.
SKILL.md lines 53-55 contain a heading and checklist items about deployment mistakes. They do not request host enumeration, credential discovery, or other system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Deployment mistakes can release untested code and break production workflows. This skill turns deployment into a local verification checklist before any release command runs.
actual_capabilities: Requires a successful local build before deployment.
Starts the local development server as part of verification.
Directs browser testing through Chrome DevTools MCP.
Requires existing tests to pass before release.
Runs production deployment only after all checklist steps pass.
limitations: Assumes the project uses pnpm and Vercel.
Does not define project-specific test coverage requirements.
Requires Chrome DevTools MCP for browser validation.
Production deployment commands still require user oversight.

use_cases.title: Validate UI Changes
use_cases.description: Run build, browser, and interaction checks before deploying a changed interface.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Gates
use_cases.description: Use one checklist so every deployment follows the same local verification steps.

use_cases.title: Control AI Deployments
use_cases.description: Prevent an AI assistant from deploying before local build and browser checks finish.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deploy skill. Check my app locally before any deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Vercel Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deploy skill before Vercel. Run the build, start the dev server, test changed flows, and report blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Review Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deploy skill for this feature branch. Focus browser testing on changed components, forms, and console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Gate Production Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the deploy skill as a release gate. Document each check result, failed assumption, and deployment decision before production release.

output_examples.output: I will verify locally first: build, local server, browser validation, and tests. Deployment waits until each check passes.

output_examples.input: The build is green, deploy now.
output_examples.output: Build success is not enough. I still need local server validation, browser interaction checks, console review, and any available tests.
All checks passed: build, local run, browser flows, and tests. I will proceed only after deployment approval is clear.

best_practices: Keep build and test scripts reliable enough to run before every deployment.
Verify changed user flows in a real browser before release.
Fix failed checklist steps before retrying deployment.
anti_patterns: Deploying immediately after a successful build.
Using production deployment to discover basic defects.
Skipping browser checks after interface or dependency changes.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It enforces a local deployment checklist before release commands run.

faq.question: Does it deploy automatically?
faq.answer: It only proceeds after the required local checks pass and deployment approval is clear.

faq.question: Which deployment tool does it mention?
faq.answer: The workflow includes Vercel production deployment after local verification.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires tests to pass when the project has tests available.

faq.question: Does it support browser testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the assistant to test changed functionality through Chrome DevTools MCP.

faq.question: What should users review before use?
faq.answer: Users should review project scripts and confirm they trust the repository before commands run.
